correctness.rationale: For each unselected vertex its multiset of distances to the selected landmarks is determined exactly by (number of selected same-part vertices, indicator that its one deleted partner is selected), since all ordinary cross distances are one, same-part distances two, deleted cross distances three for p>=3. A side may therefore have at most two unselected vertices, and two on the same side require opposite deleted-partner indicators. For three or four outside vertices the two-part same-side-distance count creates the boundary q=p+1 and prohibits four omissions when p=q; complete combinatorial case analysis gives A2=t(p+q-2t)+(pq if p<q else 2t(p-t)), A3=t(t-1)+t(p-t)(q-1)+1_(q!=p+1)[t(t-1)+t(q-t)(p-1)], A4=1_(p<q)t(t-1)[t-2+(p-t)(q-t)]. The crown p=q=t=n coefficients A2=A4=0 and A3=2n(n-1) prove the missing cardinality layer. Independently enumerated all subsets by BFS over 43 distinct parameter triples (3<=p<=5,p<=q<=6,0<=t<=p), reproducing the entire polynomial; finite tests only corroborate the all-parameter combinatorial argument.
residual_risks: The all-parameter theorem assumes p>=3, since deleted-pair distances need not stay three when smaller part has size two.
Finite BFS enumeration cannot prove the general omitted-vertex cardinality classification.
